international.summary: Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast The energy minister, Chris Bowen , has said the failed COP31 negotiations he presided over were more strained than previous years. Bowen, who served as president of negotiations at the talks in Turkiye, was interviewed on the ABC’s 7.30 program last night about the conference, which did not result in consensus among the countries over a proposed “cover decision”, or an overarching agreement, for the conference. The difference this year was countries were a lot harder to budge from their position and frankly I felt a lot of geopolitical tension in the room on other issues infecting the conversation and making it so much harder to negotiate. I’ve been to five Cops, seen plenty of argy-bargy but there was a lot more rigidness to the negotiations this year. We [Australia] have always supported transition away from fossil fuels.
